LANDING PR for story #487, ported onto decision 0065: the provisional tier. A new model is seatable only in the offices the operator lists for provisional seats, and never as a gate. Proposed decision 0075 ruling 5, epic #485, commissioned by the operator ahead of 0075's acceptance.

The branch story-487-on-0065 is a fresh port off main 2a23488b (v0.12.0 with 0065 slice one, #508 and #366) and ends at 25a6d33d. It replaces the pre-0065 branch story-487-provisional-tier (pull request #494). Commits:
- 49bf2edc: the port, under realms.v7. 0065 took v6, so the provisional offices are realms.v7, which adds only `provisional_offices`.
- 095db7d2 (first security-hold fix): an inline seat's --fallback-model is judged as link 2, and every adapter file is read strictly. A duplicate key refuses.
- 99c18c55 and eb58093c (second security-hold fix, run implement-story-487-the-provisio-1f88db0f): an adapter's own argv (the driver tail, hands.workspace, hands.harness gate and work fragments) may name no model flag, refused at adapter load. An inline pin on link 1 or 2 that is the id of no model the adapter declares is refused wherever the adapter declares a provisional model, so aliases such as `opus` are refused, not resolved. That run's review ruled residual at low. Its chief replanted every removal control.
- 25a6d33d (controller): the exact-coverage gate missed one line, bundle.rs CapabilityAdapters::of's Some(Ok) arm. The port made that arm unreachable: inline adapters that load now open an agent context. `of` became `unloaded`, which keeps only the two cases that remain. The gate is now 100% on every axis, and the host lints pass.

Judge:
1. That no path seats a provisional model in a gate or in an unlisted office. Cover inline seats (primary and --fallback-model pins, aliases, unreadable pins), agent chains, composed recipes, and argv the adapter itself supplies. That a promoted or tierless entry compiles as it did on main. That the refusal names what the operator must change.
2. That realms.v7 is additive: every v4 to v6 map still loads, and decision 0065's grants and capabilities are unchanged. Say whether frozen_contracts.rs should byte-pin v7 (the prior LOW 6; the operator rules).
3. That 25a6d33d changes no behaviour: the removed arm was unreachable, and the two remaining cases are as before.
4. That the adapter-load refusal of a model flag in adapter argv is stated where an operator reads it: docs/guides/provider-adapters.md and the release-note material (the prior LOW 5). An operator library outside this repository whose adapter tail pins a model stops loading on upgrade.
5. The prior chief's LOW 1 (a model flag inside a native capability's OFF switch argv) and LOW 2 (one id declared under aliases of two tiers) are for the operator or a follow-up. Say whether either is more than LOW.

The PR's Ruling line will name the raised baselines: doctor.rs 1567→1572, core realms.rs 902→918, agents.rs 1671→1673, agents/load.rs 1334→1335, bundle.rs 7815→7821, parse_adapter CC 198→199, and the public API (core 566→568, runtime 1373→1407). Check each is this story's and no larger than it needs.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy on the crates you touched, with -D warnings
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, crap and api

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

members.adversarial:
Reviewed the complete story delta 2a23488b..25a6d33d, including the earlier fixes, against decisions 0004, 0005, 0065 and 0071. No high/critical finding or new realistic accidental bypass found. No source changes, mutations, fixes or commits; probes used disposable /tmp library copies, removed afterwards. No provider was launched.

LOW 1, security, 0071 ruling 3: agents/load/models.rs:91-96 checks driver and the three hands fragments, but not native-capability disposition argv. Concrete reproduction: mark claude.models.opus provisional; set native_capabilities.known.web-search.off.argv to ["--disallowedTools", "WebSearch", "--fallback-model", "claude-opus-5-5"]. recipes/fast compiles (exit 0), including its inline review gate. The same fallback in driver is refused (exit 1). capabilities.rs:2100 adds this argv to the native plan; native_controls.rs:2329 includes it in final composition, and grammar.rs:478 treats the fallback flag as inert. This is a compile bypass; runtime launch was not observed. It remains LOW under the operator's 2026-09-26 threat model: a model selector inside an operator-authored capability OFF switch is an exotic evasion, not realistic accidental misuse. Follow-up: include native disposition argv in the pinless check.

LOW 2, security, 0071 ruling 5: tier.rs:233-235 judges agent links by abstract name, while :316-319 judges inline pins by concrete id. Concrete reproduction: declare opus provisional and opus-b tierless, both mapping to claude-opus-5-5; add opus-b to judges and replace agents' opus model/effort keys with opus-b. recipes/panel-review compiles (exit 0), including its gate positions; making opus-b provisional too refuses compilation (exit 1). This remains LOW: the input contradicts its own tier declaration and the story puts tier on each models entry. Follow-up: refuse conflicting tiers for aliases of one id, or judge both paths consistently by id. Neither prior LOW 1 nor LOW 2 merits elevation on the evidence found.

LOW 5, upgrade documentation (commission judge 4): provider-adapters.md:296-325 states the provisional tier but never states the unconditional adapter-load refusal or the undeclared-inline-id refusal. No release-note material changed. A tierless claude adapter whose driver tail contains --fallback-model claude-opus-5-5 now refuses to load (reproduced exit 1), so an external operator library that previously pinned models there stops compiling on upgrade without advance migration guidance. Document removing pins from adapter driver/hands fragments and putting them in seat/agent chains, and the declared-concrete-id requirement when provisional entries exist.

Compatibility and controller judgment: primary/fallback inline pins, unreadable/absent/undeclared pins, agent fallback links and composed site bodies reach the tier check; ordinary pins and driver/hands injections are refused with named seats/adapters and actionable context. Promoted/tierless controls and shipped recipes pass. realms.v7 adds only optional world-level provisional_offices; older v4-v6 loading/version gates and decision 0065 grants/capabilities remain unchanged. Frozen-byte diff contains only new realms.v7 plus contracts/README.md; no existing schema, fixture, policy or reference byte changed. On prior LOW 6, recommend byte-pinning v7 when it is published, alongside v6: the structural test does not freeze all its bytes. This is for the operator's ruling; no current v7 semantic mismatch was found. 25a6d33d changes no reachable behavior: Some(Ok) always produces an AgentContext, no code clears it, and only None/Some(Err) can reach CapabilityAdapters::unloaded; their fields match the former arms.

INFO, 0071 ruling 4, gate authority: baselines 2a23488b reports exactly doctor.rs 1567->1572, core realms.rs 902->918, agents.rs 1671->1673, agents/load.rs 1334->1335, bundle.rs 7815->7821, parse_adapter 198->199 function lines, core public API 566->568 and runtime 1373->1407. These deltas are this story's integration, version/tier data and typed refusal API; no unrelated growth found. Correct the PR's terminology: 198->199 is clippy function length, not CC (the committed parse_adapter CC baseline is 71). The baseline gate requires the stated Ruling line; it is not an additional implementation finding.

Validation run here: cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked --offline passed; cargo fmt --all -- --check, clippy for core/runtime/cli with all targets/features and -D warnings, typos --hidden, git diff --check, quality/ratchet.sh files/clones/crap/api and cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self all passed. The crap ratchet used the controller's existing target/coverage/lcov.info. Mutation-control records were inspected, not replanted in this read-only seat. scripts/coverage-exact.sh was not run. Tracked worktree stayed clean.
members.correctness:
Read-only correctness and fit review of 2a23488b..25a6d33d, all five story commits. Read README, decisions 0004, 0005 and 0071, cumulative production/test/contract/documentation/quality diffs, the prior chief ledger and commit removal-control records. No source edits, fixes, commits or launches. Result residual, maximum LOW; no correctness finding returns the branch. Security verdict belongs to the adjacent member; has_security_residual is false as this seat's contract requires.

Findings and assessments:
1. LOW, decision 0071 ruling 5: agents/load/models.rs:81 PIN_FLAGS restates --model and --fallback-model beside bundle.rs MODEL_FLAG and tier.rs FALLBACK_FLAG. One vocabulary has multiple homes; a future flag change can leave the readers disagreeing. Carry the prior chief's LOW 3.
2. LOW, ruling 9: doctor/capability_tests.rs removes the dsh-model adapter and admitted("private", "dsh-model") assertion. The unconditional adapter-load refusal forced removal of that fixture, as the implementer explains in 99c18c55, but the cited protocol overlay test does not replace a doctor-level admission assertion. Carry the prior LOW 4.
3. LOW, operator-facing fit of the refusal at the data edge (rulings 3 and 9): docs/guides/provider-adapters.md:296 explains the tier but states neither that model flags in driver/hands argv now refuse adapter load for EVERY adapter, nor that undeclared inline primary/fallback ids and aliases are refused wherever an adapter declares a provisional model. No corresponding migration notice appears in docs/releases. An external operator library with a previously valid model-pinning driver tail stops loading on upgrade, even when all its models are promoted. The guide and release-note material owe that explanation and the remedy: move the pin to the seat/agent chain. Carry prior LOW 5, knowingly left to the operator in eb58093c.
4. LOW, ruling 9 / frozen-contract requirement: frozen_contracts.rs pins v6, not v7. Its structural test proves the additive property set and several schema constraints but cannot freeze every v7 byte. I recommend byte-pinning v7 now; the implementer deliberately followed the predecessor-pinning convention, and whether to retain that convention is the operator's ruling. Carry prior LOW 6.
5. INFO, rulings 4 and 6, gate authority: quality/ratchet.sh baselines 2a23488b reports exactly doctor.rs 1567->1572, core realms.rs 902->918, agents.rs 1671->1673, agents/load.rs 1334->1335, bundle.rs 7815->7821, parse_adapter 198->199 lines, API core 566->568 and runtime 1373->1407 items. These all trace to the story's tier field, realm/version plumbing, context opening and typed refusals, with consumers; the new substantive logic is in small separate modules. The increases are modest and no unrelated baseline grows. The PR must name their operator ruling. Correction to task wording: 198->199 is parse_adapter's function LINE count in too-many-lines.txt, not CC; crap-baseline.json retains its cyclomatic baseline 71 and is unchanged.
6. INFO, ruling 9, carried prior chief observation: a_shipped_recipe_is_refused_once_its_adapter_tail_names_a_model matches CompileError::Invalid then checks a message prefix. It binds to both shipped recipe refusals, with a compiling removal control recorded, but does not pin the entire text there; the fragment test pins the full shared refusal. No nonbinding new test found.

Requested security-adjacent assessments (notes only; the security member owns the verdict):
7. LOW, ruling 3, prior LOW 1: pinless reads driver, hands.workspace, hands.harness.gate and work, but not native capability switch argv.
